longStrings.long.faq.a1: Your username is your national ID number, and your password is generated randomly by the system and sent via the Shad messenger to your registered number. For all users — from the school principal to the student — the sign-in method is the same. After your first login, change your password from the profile section; this is required for account security.
longStrings.long.faq.a10: Alongside the final report card, Bahar builds a monthly performance summary for every student: the average of that month's grades, that month's attendance and absence days, and its assignments. This summary is shown to the student and the parent in the grades section so that month-by-month progress is visible.
longStrings.long.faq.a1NoShad: Your username is your national ID number, and your password is generated randomly by the system and handed to you by the school principal. For all users — from the school principal to the student — the sign-in method is the same. After your first login, change your password from the profile section; this is required for account security.
longStrings.long.faq.a2: Contact your school principal. From the users panel, the principal can generate a new random password for you and send it to you via Shad. Passwords are stored encrypted and no one — not even the principal — can see your current password; only generating a new one is possible.
longStrings.long.faq.a2NoShad: Contact your school principal. From the users panel, the principal can generate a new random password for you and hand it to you. Passwords are stored encrypted and no one — not even the principal — can see your current password; only generating a new one is possible.
longStrings.long.faq.a3: The built-in messenger is designed only for short, light messages so that the system's server always stays fast. To send files, photos and large content, use the Shad messenger; Bahar reminds you of this very point in the built-in messenger.
longStrings.long.faq.a3NoShad: The built-in messenger is designed only for short, light messages so that the system's server always stays fast. To send files, photos and large content, use common communication tools; Bahar reminds you of this very point in the built-in messenger.
longStrings.long.faq.a4: The web version runs in every browser, and this same version installs as an app on Android and Windows — one account, three platforms. The Android version is also provided to the school as a standalone APK file.
longStrings.long.faq.a5: Passwords are generated with a cryptographically secure generator and stored as hashes. After a few failed attempts the account is temporarily locked, and changing the password after the first login is mandatory. Bahar never keeps any password in plain text.
longStrings.long.faq.a6: The student record contains the student's own complete information as well as the guardian's full details (name, national ID, phone number and Shad number). Teacher, deputy and principal records likewise hold their own complete details. Access to each record is granted only to authorized roles.
longStrings.long.faq.a6NoShad: The student record contains the student's own complete information as well as the guardian's full details (name, national ID and phone number). Teacher, deputy and principal records likewise hold their own complete details. Access to each record is granted only to authorized roles.
longStrings.long.faq.a7: When creating or editing each deputy and teacher, the school principal specifies exactly which sections they can access — such as entering grades, attendance, student management or events. Every access change takes effect immediately and is logged in the activity report.
longStrings.long.faq.a8: The school principal connects their Shad account to the system once; from then on, Bahar sends every new user's username and password to their registered Shad number. This is only a convenience side feature, and if it is not connected, the principal delivers the password to the user another way.
longStrings.long.faq.a9: Yes. Besides installing directly from the browser, Bahar's Android project file is provided to the school and can easily be converted to an APK with Android Studio — no need for Google Play.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.algoNote: The example field must actually pass its algorithm — pack validation checks it (a fake national ID = rejected pack).
longStrings.long.kit.countries.calNote: Important: attendance date keys are stored with the active calendar (Iran: "1404-07-10" in the Solar Hijri calendar; Gregorian: "2025-10-08"). Activate the country pack before the school year starts so the keys are consistent from day one. Existing calendar data is not converted automatically (this limitation is documented explicitly).
longStrings.long.kit.countries.cta: Download the template, fill the fields with your country's values, and upload it in Settings → the "Country" tab. Validation is precise and guides you through. Returning to Iran is always one click away.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.fieldIntro: Each table below is one section of the JSON file. The "Iran value" column is exactly what you see in the template — model your file on it and follow the "Rule" column for your country.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.hero: Every nationality-dependent feature — calendar, national ID, mobile numbers, provinces and counties, map, currency, grade levels and work week — lives in one JSON file. The default country is Iran; once a country pack is uploaded, the whole system works with your country's details.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.mapIntro: Bahar's Iran map is built from GADM 4.1 with Douglas-Peucker simplification — run the same pipeline for your country:
longStrings.long.kit.countries.mapNote: The map is included in the Iran template (for reference) — look at it and model yours on it. Everything also works without a map; region selection just falls back to a dropdown.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.mapStep1: Download the GeoJSON of your country's province borders from GADM / Natural Earth / OSM (ADM1 level).
longStrings.long.kit.countries.mapStep2: With mapshaper.org or a simple simplification script, turn each province into a light SVG path (under 30KB).
longStrings.long.kit.countries.mapStep3: For each province: { name, d, cx, cy } — d is the SVG path (starting with M), cx/cy the center for the hover label.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.mapStep4: Set the viewBox from the overall bounds (Iran's is 760×688).
longStrings.long.kit.countries.mapStep5: Add the map section to the JSON — if each province's name matches one of the regions names, clicking the map selects that province.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.step1: The template.json file is exactly the Iran profile — 31 provinces and 429 counties, Solar Hijri calendar, mod-11 national ID, 09… mobile numbers, Toman, grades 7 to 12, and a Saturday-to-Wednesday week. Replace each field with your country's values.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.step2: Below each section of this page, the fields are documented with type, range and Iran's example. A missing field = the pack fails validation (you get a precise Persian error).
longStrings.long.kit.countries.step3: Put provinces/states + counties into regions. If you also want an SVG map, build paths from your country's official GeoJSON with Douglas-Peucker simplification (exact instructions at the bottom of this page). The map is optional — without it, only the dropdown is shown.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.step4: The super admin uploads the file in Settings → the "Country" tab. Dry-run validation (?validate=1) checks the structure, calendar, regexes, regions and map and gives stats — errors are precise and in Persian.
longStrings.long.kit.countries.step5: With "Activate", the whole system's calendar (date display + attendance keys), national ID/mobile validation at login and sign-up, province and grade dropdowns, currency and work week all switch to the new country. Returning to Iran is always one click away.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.cta: Download the template, translate it, and have it activated by the system admin — all your users can pick the new language immediately.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.hero: Bahar's UI is Persian by default — but with a "language pack" you can translate the whole panel into any language: English, Arabic, Turkish, Kurdish, Gilaki, Balochi, or your school's local language. The JSON structure is simple, partial translation is allowed, and untranslated keys fall back to Persian. For a quick start, download the ready-made English pack (200 app keys; site strings and long texts in progress) and use it as a model.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.step1: Download Bahar's official template file — it contains every translatable key with the standard JSON structure and an in-file guide.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.step2: Translate each key's Persian text into the target language. Keys you do not translate can be removed — those items automatically fall back to Persian and nothing breaks.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.step3: Write the unique language code (e.g. en or kurdish-sorani), the Persian name, the native name and the text direction (rtl/ltr) in the fields at the top of the file.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.step4: The super admin uploads the file in Settings → "Languages & Translation"; the system validates it, measures the coverage percentage and activates the pack.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.step5: As soon as it is activated, the new language appears in every user's language picker (web, Android, Windows) and the UI direction is set automatically.
longStrings.long.kit.languages.structureNote: Packs are validated before being stored (field types, text lengths, absence of executable code), and only the system's super admin can upload and activate them. Text rendering always goes through safe HTML escaping.
